int_name: N 8TH ST & VINE STREET EXPY RAMP 8061A

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is located under a wide highway overpass, characterized by poor lighting and a lack of marked crossings. While sidewalks are present, they are narrow and lack separation from the roadway, and signage explicitly prohibits pedestrian crossing at this location.

hazards.name: Poor Lighting
hazards.description: The area under the overpass is significantly darker than the surrounding environment, reducing visibility of pedestrians to drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossing
hazards.description: Despite sidewalks being present, there is no marked crosswalk across the multi-lane roadway, and a stop bar is the only marking.

hazards.name: Prohibitive Signage
hazards.description: A 'No Pedestrian Crossing' sign is present, which may force pedestrians to take longer routes or cross in unsafe conditions.
hazards.location_in_image: Pole on the left side of the image

interventions.title: Under-bridge Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-intensity LED lighting under the bridge structure to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: If crossing is to be permitted, install continental-style crosswalk markings and appropriate signage to formalize the pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffering
interventions.description: Add a physical buffer or bollards between the narrow sidewalk and the travel lanes to protect pedestrians from vehicle splash and proximity.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked crosswalk with a curb ramp and tactile paving, situated next to a large bridge structure. While basic infrastructure is present, the one-way traffic flow and visual obstructions from the bridge wall may impact pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The bridge abutment on the left limits sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, the concrete wall under the bridge.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra stripes are beginning to wear, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extension
interventions.description: Install a curb extension on the left corner to shorten the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and marked crosswalks. The environment is dominated by wide asphalt surfaces and multi-lane traffic, which results in long crossing distances for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway at the intersection requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a refuge.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radius
hazards.description: The curb radius on the left corner appears wide, which can facilitate higher-speed vehicle turns.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the wide crossing to allow pedestrians to cross in stages and reduce exposure.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and slow turning traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace standard parallel line markings with continental or ladder style markings for better visibility to drivers.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked zebra crosswalk and wide sidewalks, but is situated in a car-centric area near highway infrastructure. The lack of pedestrian signals and the wide, open roadway design suggest a higher risk for pedestrians despite the basic infrastructure present.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks a pedestrian signal or stop control, requiring pedestrians to judge gaps in traffic from the ramp.

hazards.name: High-Speed Environment
hazards.description: The proximity to highway ramps and wide lane widths encourages higher vehicle speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway leading to and from the overpass

interventions.title: Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon
interventions.description: Install a signal to provide a protected crossing phase for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility by extending the curb into the roadway.

interventions.title: Advanced Warning Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Pedestrian Crossing' signs with flashing beacons to alert drivers.
